business_scope.primary_industry_name: International Brokerage of Ginned Raw Cotton and Synthetic Yarns

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: AML/CFT and UBO governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17, together with its regulations (FINTRAC regime); Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44, ss 21.1-21.4 (individuals with significant control) and S.C. 2023, c 26, operational 22 January 2024 (federal beneficial ownership transparency registry); provincial post-incorporation UBO filings for limited partnerships under Ontario Limited Partnerships Act, RSO 1990, c L.7, British Columbia Partnership Act, RSBC 1996, c 348, and Alberta Partnership Act, RSA 2000, c P-3, each as amended; criminal and sanctions statutes: Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, ss 462.31 and 83.03; Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17; United Nations Act, RSC 1985, c U-2; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Sergei Magnitsky Act), SC 2017, c 21; tax-law regard to Income Tax Act, RSC 1985, c 1 (5th Supp.), as amended.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of foreign general partner's certificate of incorporation or registry extract proving legal existence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-jurisdiction corporate registry (e.g., Companies House, Delaware Division of Corporations, Registrar of Companies of the partner's state)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the competent authority of the document's origin state; if origin state is not a 1961 Hague Convention member, full consular legalization through the nearest Canadian foreign mission

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board resolution or written consent of the foreign general partner authorizing formation, capitalization, and bank account opening of the Canadian Limited Partnership
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary of the foreign general partner with notarial attestation of corporate books
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a local notary, followed by Hague Apostille; consular legalization chain required for non-Hague states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Compliance (aged certificate) of the foreign general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent registry of the general partner's incorporation jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; country-of-origin sequential consular legalization where required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Statutory declaration of ultimate beneficial ownership, source of funds, and absence of PEP or sanctions status executed by each UBO of the Limited Partnership
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or commissioner of oaths in the UBO's jurisdiction of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille; consular legalization chain for non-Hague origin states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney and registered-office acceptance undertaking appointing a Canadian attorney for service
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign general partner and Canadian registered agent; notarized signature of the grantor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization of foreign signature; if executed in Canada, apostille via Global Affairs Canada for use in extra-provincial filings

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA), R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, ss. 5, 8, 10, 101, 106, 213 for the corporate general partner; applicable provincial Limited Partnerships Act (e.g., Limited Partnerships Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. L.16) for the limited partnership registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada, for the federal corporate general partner; provincial limited partnerships registry for the limited partnership.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (CBCA Form 1) for the corporate general partner; Declaration of Limited Partnership or equivalent provincial form for the LP.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is prescribed; no escrow account is required. The limited partner may contribute capital in cash or property as specified in the partnership agreement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that this first board meeting of [Corporate General Partner] Inc. approves the subscription and issuance of one common share to the sole incorporator, adopts the registered office at [Address], and appoints [Name] as President and [Name] as Corporate Secretary, each effective immediately, with authority to execute all filings, banking resolutions, and applications required for the formation and registration of the related limited partnership. FURTHER RESOLVED, that management is authorized to file all necessary formation documents, pay all statutory fees, retain counsel and accountants, and certify that the partnership’s capital contributions and business scope comply with the Canada Business Corporations Act and the Limited Partnerships Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre via a NUANS-approved search house
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS name search for the proposed corporate general partner and, where applicable, verify the limited partnership name with the provincial registry. If the name is distinctive and not confusingly similar, reserve the corporate name through the online portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, submit a revised name search with a new name within five business days; the original filing fee is not refunded.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of Partnership Agreement and General Partner Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal counsel and corporate records office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the limited partnership agreement, including capital contributions, profit-sharing ratios, and general partner authority. Prepare CBCA Form 1 Articles of Incorporation for the corporate general partner reflecting one class of common shares and the registered office address.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the articles are incomplete, Corporations Canada issues a notice of default; correct and refile the articles or amended articles within the cure period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal Incorporation and Provincial Limited Partnership Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre; provincial limited partnerships registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Articles of Incorporation with Corporations Canada and pay the statutory fee. After issuance of the federal Certificate of Incorporation, register the limited partnership with the provincial registry by submitting the Declaration of Limited Partnership and paying the registration fee.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation of the general partner
Registered office address of the LP
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If provincial registration is queried due to a name conflict or missing consent, amend the declaration and refile within ten business days to avoid cancellation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office and Statutory Records Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada and provincial limited partnerships registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Establish the registered office at a physical address acceptable under the CBCA and the provincial LP legislation. File the Notice of Registered Office and maintain the register of members, register of directors, and copies of the partnership agreement at the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered office address is rejected, provide a valid street address and refile; no substantive cure beyond address correction is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Canada Revenue Agency and Program Account Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency Business Registration Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the partnership and its corporate general partner with the Canada Revenue Agency to obtain a Business Number. Apply for federal GST/HST, payroll, and import/export program accounts. Raw cotton bales exported from Canada are zero-rated for GST/HST purposes under the Excise Tax Act.
required_dossiers: Form RC1 – Request for a Business Number
Identification of general partner and principal officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA registration is rejected due to information mismatch, correct the legal name or address in the underlying corporate and partnership records and resubmit RC1.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for pure brokerage of raw cotton; if physical warehousing is later added, the local municipal business licensing office and provincial authorities may become competent.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No operating or manufacturing licence is required for export brokerage of ginned raw cotton under ISIC 4620; optional exporter identification can be obtained from Statistics Canada for trade reporting.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – no environmental impact assessment is required for office-based brokerage or trading activity. If physical cotton bale warehousing is added, a screening may be required under the Impact Assessment Act, 2019.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for pure trade. For any future warehousing activity, comply with the Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999, including dust control, waste handling standards, and prohibition of uncontrolled discharge into water or air.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No fire safety or structural inspection clearance is required for an office-based brokerage operation. If warehousing or handling facilities are established, obtain local fire safety certification, structural occupancy load inspection, and provincial workers’ compensation coverage clearance (WSIB or provincial WCB).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada; official portal: CRA My Business Account at canada.ca and GST/HST NETFILE
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Register the Canadian limited partnership under the applicable provincial Limited Partnership Act, then apply to CRA for a Business Number (BN) using Form RC1 'Request for a Business Number' or CRA Business Registration Online. Select the entity type 'Partnership' and open a GST/HST program account (RT) in the name of the LP; if export reporting is required, add an export/import program account. Provide the LP's extra-provincial registration certificate, general partner identifiers, and the non-resident limited partners' foreign tax identification numbers. CRA issues a unique 9-digit BN plus program account numbers; this BN is the statutory Canadian TIN for income tax, GST/HST and customs purposes. The LP must file Form T5013 partnership information return annually even though it is fiscally transparent.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not provide a US-style check-the-box election. The Canadian LP is fiscally transparent by default; no election permits entity-level income taxation. For GST/HST the LP is treated as a separate person and may voluntarily register as a small supplier; it may also elect to file through a specified appointing representative. Anti-hybrid rules in the Income Tax Act apply automatically; no election is available to avoid the deemed treatment of certain partnership hybrid mismatch payments.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST), a value-added tax administered federally under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of taxable supplies made in Canada in the preceding four calendar quarters (small-supplier threshold); zero-rated export supplies count toward the threshold but the export supply itself is zero-rated, and a below-threshold LP may register voluntarily.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or government-blessed continuous controls for e-invoicing in Canada. GST/HST registrants must issue invoices containing the prescribed particulars under the Excise Tax Act and retain books and records, making them available to CRA on request. Returns are filed electronically through GST/HST NETFILE or certified software; Pan-Canadian or Peppol e-invoicing is voluntary.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A supply of raw cotton bales is zero-rated under Schedule VI Part V of the Excise Tax Act when the goods are exported from Canada in the course of the supply, the goods are delivered to a destination outside Canada, and the supplier retains satisfactory evidence of export. The Canadian LP acting as principal or as disclosed agent for a non-resident principal may claim 0% GST/HST on the export sale or on the zero-rated brokerage service supplied to a non-resident recipient, provided the service is not an excepted service related to Canadian real estate or tangible personal property. The LP must have a valid GST/HST registration number and must substantiate the export within its records before claiming input tax credits or refunds.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Customs Export Declaration filed through the Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS)
Bill of Lading or equivalent air waybill showing port of exit and foreign destination
Commercial invoice / Canada Customs Invoice describing the raw cotton bales, value, goods description, and Incoterms
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank remittance advice evidencing receipt of export proceeds from the non-resident buyer
Container/booking records, terminal receipts, or shipping company documentation evidencing physical movement out of Canada
Export contract/purchase order confirming the non-resident customer and the export terms
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess a claimed zero-rated export as taxable at 5% GST if the supporting export and currency-receipt evidence is missing or conflicting, and may apply arrears interest from the date the GST was originally due. A false statement or omission on a GST/HST return can draw a penalty under section 285.1 of the Excise Tax Act, and gross negligence or wilful evasion can result in enhanced penalties and criminal prosecution. If the 180-day inward remittance/evidence deadline is not met, the zero-rating may be clawed back, input tax credits disallowed, and the exporter may be liable for unpaid GST, interest, and penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), operating with the Department of Finance Canada under the Currency Act and the Financial Administration Act; prudential regulation of all federally incorporated banks and foreign bank branches is vested in the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); AML transaction surveillance is conducted by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC); tax-related foreign-payment administration is administered by the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is freely convertible on both current and capital account, fully floating, and Canada satisfies IMF Article VIII convertibility obligations. No capital controls, no prior central-bank authorization for inbound or outbound transfers, and no repatriation licence or registration procedure exist. A limited partnership brokerage distributing commission income to non-resident partners is subject only to Part XIII Canadian withholding tax (default 25%; generally 15% under the Canada-United States Income Tax Convention where a US partner files Form NR302 for a reduced rate and provides the beneficial-ownership declaration). Capital contributions are not subject to withholding; however, any remittance of proceeds must be supported by the underlying trade documentation to satisfy the bank's purpose-of-payment requirement under FINTRAC regulations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Canada imposes no statutory surrender timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio into CAD, and no deadline for repatriation of export proceeds. The LP may retain the full foreign-currency balance in domestic or non-resident accounts. Receipts must be recorded in the CRA partnership financial statements on an accrual basis, and all foreign-currency gains and losses are computed under subsection 39(1) of the Income Tax Act. No surrender certificate or customs-linked settlement proof is demanded beyond the ordinary GST/HST zero-rating export evidence (commercial invoice, bill of lading, and proof of export within the prescribed claim period).

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Moderate-to-low for core treasury custody. Canada has no European-style EMI licence; non-bank payment providers operate as money services businesses (MSBs) registered with FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act and as payment service providers under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA, in force November 2024). Wise Canada, Payoneer, and Stripe are viable for small-value supplier payouts and commission receipts (practical C$50,000-per-transaction threshold), but they cannot open statutory trust or escrow accounts, issue documentary letters of credit, provide CDIC-insured deposit custody, or host LC settlement flows. Without a Bank Act Schedule I licence, such entities cannot take demand-deposit liabilities; therefore the primary settlement rail must remain a Schedule I bank. If the LP itself deals in foreign currency for clients, a registered MSB designation with FINTRAC and an RPAA licence are required before any fintech rails are used.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory mandate for physical attendance. All six Schedule I banks permit fully remote or hybrid onboarding for an extra-provincial limited partnership where the general partner is a corporation or non-resident, provided that: (i) the general partner completes a video-conference KYC interview with the relationship manager; (ii) certified true copies of the partnership agreement, extra-provincial registration certificate, general-partner resolution, and register of partners with beneficial ownership above 25% are delivered; and (iii) non-resident director documents are notarized or apostilled. In practice, at least one authorized signatory must complete account-opening resolution procedures at branch level. Trade-focused banks (Scotiabank, RBC) will accept a consular-attested identity form and a bank-guaranteed signature specimen from the general partner's home jurisdiction. Where any partner resides in a FATF grey-listed jurisdiction, in-person identity verification at a Canadian consulate or a bank-correspondent branch is effectively mandated.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident partners and remote signatories; the LP acts purely as a commission intermediary with no Canadian fixed premises, payroll, or inventory (shell or mailbox risk).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: General partner's certificate of good standing from its home registry; original LP agreement and extra-provincial registration certificate; register of partners with full ownership percentages; 12-month Canadian business plan with forecasted turnover; executed agreement with a Canadian freight forwarder or trade agent; reference letter from a regulated foreign bank issued within 6 months; and three years of audited or reviewed financial statements of the general partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity pass-through transactions: commission receipts and escrowed trade funds moving through the operating account without a matching invoice trail, indicating layering or sanctions evasion.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Segregation of the client-settlement escrow account from the operating profit account; signed brokerage mandate per shipment; underlying seller-buyer contract; original commercial invoice; bill of lading and CBSA cargo control documentation; GST/HST-registered commission invoice; and a monthly reconciliation statement certified by the compliance officer and submitted to the bank's financial-crimes unit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Raw-cotton origin from sanctioned or forced-labour jurisdictions (e.g., Xinjiang-origin lint subject to US UFLPA import embargoes, Syrian or North Korean export restrictions, or counterparties on OSC/OFAC/CFSP sanctions lists administered through Global Affairs Canada).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CBSA import-export declaration records; verifiable cotton-certificate chain comprising USDA/GACC phytosanitary certificates and cotton-grade certificates; Global Affairs Canada export-control screening clearance demonstrating the cotton is not on the Canadian Export Control List; forced-labour due-diligence questionnaire and supply-chain attestation aligning with Bill S-211 expectations; and third-party sanctions-screening certificate covering all counterparty beneficial owners from a reputable commercial database.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection funded by a non-resident partner from crypto-derived, cash-heavy, or unverified sources, followed by rapid conversion into USD and onward payment without CRA explanation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-wealth and source-of-funds declaration executed under penalty; 12 months of bank statements for the contributing partner and its corporate parent; tax identification documentation and, where applicable, Form NR602 partnership allocation schedule; the USD purchase contract demonstrating legitimate FX rationale; and the SWIFT MT103 confirming purpose code CAPT (capital transaction) or EGCP (equity participation).

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident partner contributions enter through SWIFT MT103 with an ISO 20022 purpose code such as CAPT (capital transfer) or EGCP (equity participation), naming the LP's registered partnership identity and CA-FED jurisdiction in the remittance information. For CAD-denominated contributions, the receiving Schedule I bank clears funds through Payments Canada Lynx (the LVTS successor) high-value real-time rail with immediate finality. All inbound electronic funds transfers above C$10,000 are subject to FINTRAC EFT reporting; the bank will hold the account until a capital-contribution schedule, partnership-agreement excerpt, and general-partner resolution are placed on file. A capital contribution is not taxable to the partnership under CRA folio S4-F6-C1, must be allocated to the contributing partner's adjusted cost base, and carries no Part XIII withholding exposure unless subsequently distributed as income to a non-resident.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: International cotton-settlement and buyer-payment operations are executed over three complementary rails: (1) SWIFT MT103/MT199 for flat commission disbursements, refunds, and operational expenses, with correspondent clearing in USD through CHIPS/Fedwire and CAD through Lynx; (2) documentary Letters of Credit issued or confirmed by a Schedule I bank trade desk using SWIFT MT700/MT707 series, subject to UCP 600, where the LP is beneficiary or arranging bank and the cotton-bale export is evidenced by presentation of the original bill of lading, certificate of origin, weight/packing list, commercial invoice, and phytosanitary certificate; and (3) documentary collections under URC 522 using SWIFT MT798/MQ messaging for works against payment or acceptance. The LP must maintain a separate trade account margined at 20-100% of each LC face amount depending on the facility agreement, must preserve all disbursement invoices for CRA foreign-transaction reporting where any transaction exceeds C$10,000, and should execute USD conversion on the bank's trading desk with an agreed all-in spread of 10-30 basis points at wholesale volumes.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: OTC CAD/USD deliverable forwards under ISDA 2013 documentation, standard tenors of 1 to 12 months, exempt from mandatory clearing and initial-margin requirements as a non-financial counterparty below the OSFI margin-rule threshold, provided the notional is directly tied to cotton-trade invoicing.
CAD/USD FX swaps (spot-start and forward-start principal exchanges) for rolling inventory turnover and working-capital bridging between inbound commission receipts and outbound supplier payments.
Cross-currency basis swaps for long-horizon cotton purchase agreements with foreign producers or buyers, tenors up to 24 months, documented under ISDA/CSA.
Exchange-traded CAD/USD futures and options on CME and the Montreal Exchange (Bourse de Montréal), preferred for transparent price discovery and elimination of bilateral counterparty credit risk.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are legally permissible under Canadian law and OSFI guidance, but are economically unnecessary because CAD is a fully deliverable G10 currency; the LP should contract in deliverable forwards unless a counterparty jurisdiction cannot effect physical CAD delivery, in which case an NDF with a Canadian Schedule I counterparty is the fallback.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return (T5013 Summary and partner slips)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of the partnership's fiscal period; for a calendar-year LP, by June 30 of the following calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty under subsection 162(8) of the Income Tax Act: the greater of CAD 250 per month (maximum CAD 2,500) and 5% of the aggregate reportable income/loss amounts on T5013 slips; continued failure may lead to CRA prosecution and compliance action. No administrative strike-off arises solely from CRA tax filing delinquency.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST return (annual or periodic, if the LP is a registrant making taxable supplies in Canada)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual filers: within three months after the end of the GST/HST fiscal year; monthly and quarterly filers: within one month after the end of the reporting period.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of net tax owing plus 1% for each full month late, up to 12 months, plus daily interest on unpaid amounts; habitual non-filing may lead to CRA collection enforcement, including liens and legal proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T106 Information Return for Transactions with Non-Resident Related Persons (if applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due at the same time as the T5013 Partnership Information Return, generally within six months after the end of the fiscal period; for a calendar-year LP, by June 30 of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty under subsection 162(7.2) of the Income Tax Act of CAD 100 per day from the date the return was required to be filed until filed, subject to a maximum of CAD 2,500; false or incomplete reporting may also attract accuracy penalties.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory independent audit is imposed on a Canadian limited partnership by the Income Tax Act or by applicable provincial limited partnership legislation based solely on revenue or asset size. A certified audit is compulsory only if the LP is a reporting issuer under Canadian securities legislation, is registered as an investment fund, is a tax shelter identified by CRA for audit verification, or if the partnership agreement, lender, or export credit agency requires audited financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: CPA Canada Handbook – Accounting: Part I (IFRS) for publicly accountable entities; Part II (ASPE) for private and owner-managed limited partnerships. Financial statements are not required to be filed with CRA unless specifically requested, but the LP's records must be sufficient to compute income under the Income Tax Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: There is no separate federal annual UBO confirmation return for a limited partnership. The general partner must maintain and update the register of limited partners within 15 days of any admission, withdrawal, transfer or pledge of a limited-partner interest, and must annually report each partner's share and allocation on the T5013 schedule. If the LP is a FINTRAC reporting entity, beneficial ownership must be verified at the 25% threshold at client onboarding and re-verified every two years or whenever a change of control is identified.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited Partners (names, addresses, contributions, transfers, withdrawals)
Minute book of general-partner resolutions and limited-partner consents
